question.prompt: Let \(N\) be a positive multiple of \(5.\) One red ball and \(N\) green balls are arranged in a line in random order. Let \(P(N)\) be the probability that at least \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of the green balls are on the same side of the red ball. Observe that \(P(5)=1\) and that \(P(N)\) approaches \(\dfrac{4}{5}\) as \(N\) grows large. What is the sum of the digits of the least value of \(N\) such that \(P(N)\lt\dfrac{321}{400}?\)

solutions.explanation:
Only the red ball's position matters. Its \(N+1\) possible positions are equally likely. If \(j\) green balls lie to its left, then \(N-j\) lie to its right, where \(j\) can be any integer from \(0\) through \(N\).

At least \(3N/5\) green balls are on one side exactly when
\[
j\geq \frac{3N}{5}
\quad\text{or}\quad
j\leq \frac{2N}{5}.
\]
Because \(N\) is a positive multiple of \(5\), these endpoints are integers and the two ranges do not overlap. Each range contains \(2N/5+1\) values, including both endpoints. Consequently,
\[
P(N)=\frac{4N/5+2}{N+1}.
\]

Now \(N+1>0\), so multiplying the required inequality by \(400(N+1)\) preserves its direction:
\[
\frac{4N/5+2}{N+1}<\frac{321}{400}
\]
\[
320N+800<321N+321.
\]
Thus \(N>479\). The least allowed multiple of \(5\) is \(480\), and its digit sum is
\[
4+8+0=\boxed{12},
\]
which is choice \(\text{A}\).
solutions.title: Count the red ball's positions
